summary: A cardholder makes purchases within the credit limit, receives a statement, and then posts a payment after the due date that is less than the required minimum. This scenario exercises the late-payment path, showing that the minimum-payment obligation is not satisfied on time while still including the modeled credit-limit and grace-period obligations in the timeline.
assumptions: The billing cycle closes on 2025-05-31 and the statement sets a payment due date of 2025-06-25.
The new balance on the 2025-05-31 statement is $600.00, so the minimum payment is 3% of the new balance, or $18.00, because that exceeds $15.00.
There is no previous balance before this cycle, so the issuer's grace-period obligation applies to new purchases in this cycle.
All card activity remains below the $1,000.00 credit limit, so the credit-limit obligation is performed and not breached in this scenario.

The only payment in this scenario is a $10.00 payment posted on 2025-06-27, which is after the due date and below the required $18.00 minimum; therefore the minimum-payment obligation is treated as unmet for the statement period.

Because the payment is late, the account follows the contract's late-payment/default path; any resulting fee or default consequence is part of the narrative outcome even though those consequences are not among the required bound obligation clause ids.
